subject: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals - HealthSystems
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harris <ben.harris@healthsystems.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals - HealthSystems

Hi Ben -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're all aligned and to capture next steps. Happy to adjust anything that's missing.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Lack of fine-grained observability for model regressions (hard to tie regressions to prompt changes).
- No centralized dashboards for per-route quality/latency and token cost.
- Need tracing hooks to correlate inference requests back to request metadata (customer id, model variant, routing policy).
- Concerned about silent quality degradation during rollouts.

Current stack:
- Frontend: React web + Node.js backend calling a mix of managed APIs and in-house proxies.
- Logging: Splunk for infra logs, Datadog for metrics.
- Model/serving: trialing multiple hosted/open models; no dedicated eval harness today.

Success criteria for the eval/pilot:
- Visibility: dashboards showing per-route quality (heuristic scoring) and latency/cost breakdowns within 48 hours of deployment.
- Regression detection: alerts on statistically significant drops for golden prompt sets.
- Tracing: ability to trace a failing customer request back to prompt, model variant, and routing policy.
- Rollout guardrails: an automated canary with rollback on quality regressions.

What we'll deliver for the pilot (proposal):
- Pre-built Redwood dashboards (cost, latency, per-prompt quality) populated with a week of historical test traffic.
- Tracing hook integration guide + sample instrumentation for Node.js.
- Golden prompt set template (attached) + initial set we'll seed with you for regression monitoring.
- Regression alerting rules and a suggested canary rollout config.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) You'll share a set of 30-50 golden prompts and one sample traffic log (PII scrubbed) for seeding dashboards.
2) We'll provision a short-lived eval workspace and populate dashboards for review.
3) Schedule a 60-minute demo next week to walk the dashboards and proposed rollout flows.
4) Procurement will need an initial SOW + pilot pricing (Jonas and Rachel will follow up).

Attachments: HealthSystems-MAVP-Eval-Checklist.xlsx (eval checklist), redwood-evals-template.csv (golden prompt template).

Open questions (from our side):
- Are there any regulatory constraints (e.g., off-shore model execution) we should be aware of?
- Preferred date/time windows next week for the demo?

Thanks - looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Harris <ben.harris@healthsystems.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, procurement@healthsystems.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals - HealthSystems

Marissa - thanks for the clear write-up, this looks accurate. A few clarifications and items from our side:

- Compliance: we need assurance that any logs used for evals do not leave our VPC or include PHI. If production or real patient data is needed, it must be processed in our GovCloud region.
- Golden prompts: we can share an initial set of ~40 prompts but will scrub PHI. We'll also include expected outputs for regression comparisons.
- SOC2: procurement asked if you can provide a short SOC2 summary + where we can view audit controls.
- Pilot scope & pricing: procurement wants a 30-day pilot with up to 1M tokens/month and a fixed pilot fee. Please put together an SOW and pilot pricing (Jonas, Rachel - can you coordinate on the SOW?).
- Timeline: we're available for the demo next Wednesday or Thursday morning (10/13 or 10/14) between 09:00-12:00 PT.

If you can include a short plan showing how regressions are detected (metric thresholds, statistical test, and sample alert emails), that would help speed approvals.

Thanks - looping procurement here.

Ben Harris
Director, Applied AI
HealthSystems Inc
ben.harris@healthsystems.com
